topic: what a Friday release checklist really needs

grades.notes:
coverage: 5 atoms across 4 types (number x2, mechanism, limit, object): the risk, the answer, the form, the outcome
specificity: each atom carries a figure or a named thing: 70%, 5 to 9 items, 19 items in three pauses of 7, 7 and 5, 1.5% to 0.8% in 8 hospitals
sourced: every row names a published work: the Google SRE book introduction, Gawande ch. 6, the WHO checklist, Haynes et al. NEJM 2009
surprise: atom 4 is not about software at all: a surgical checklist built around three stops, which a release list can borrow

novelty: operator 1 (put to another use): a surgical form becomes the release list; similar reports no overlap with memory, which is empty
truth: every number is sourced: 19 items in pauses of 7, 7 and 5 (WHO 2009), 5 to 9 per pause (Gawande ch. 6), 1.5% to 0.8% (Haynes 2009)
relevance: a Friday release list grows past nine lines; the form that keeps each stop under nine is what the list needs
intrigue: an operating theatre's form as the answer to a deploy question opens a gap the reader wants closed
tone: plain and factual; it does not claim software outages fall like surgical deaths, only that the form transfers

coherence: specimen-label lends the catalogue's dry facts; the quote layout puts the anomaly hook at display size and the WHO form small as its attribution
feasibility: one page, the brand's own faces and colours, the object is three rows of boxes from atom 4, all local fonts, no picture needed
